clue.text: Scientist has to regret going back behind history

indicators.note: behind places the turned regret after the word for history

parts.note: history is the past

indicators.note: going back tells us to read the word for regret from right to left

parts.note: to regret is to rue

explanation.surface: A scientist laments as he looks back over the past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going back' turns RUE into EUR, and 'behind' puts it after PAST.
explanation.definitionFit: Louis Pasteur was the French chemist and microbiologist who pioneered pasteurisation and vaccines.

clue.text: Light vehicle appearing in bad epic

indicators.note: appearing in signals the letters of the two following words turning up in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A small cart features in a poor historical film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appearing in' is the anagram signal: the seven letters of BAD EPIC are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedicab is a pedal-powered cycle rickshaw, a light passenger vehicle.

clue.text: Always in a rush one after the other

indicators.note: in places the word for always inside the word for a rush

parts.note: a sally is a sudden rush out, a sortie
always means ever

explanation.surface: Constantly hurrying, things happen in quick succession.
explanation.walkthrough: SALLY, a sudden charge out from a besieged place, is cut open by 'in' to take EVER.
explanation.definitionFit: Severally means separately or individually, each taken in turn.

clue.text: Stays short of a hundred and relaxes

indicators.note: short of means lacking, so the hundred is dropped from the word for stays

parts.note: stays in the sense of stops or halts, ceases
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: Someone stays put, falling short of a century, and takes it easy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stays' means stops, CEASES, not remains; losing C (100) leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To ease is to relax or slacken, so the third-person forms match.

clue.text: A rogue may be included in or a scallywag

indicators.note: included in says the letters sit inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A villain might be counted among the scoundrels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'included in' signals the letters lying inside 'or a scallywag'.
explanation.definitionFit: A rascal is a mischievous or dishonest person, a rogue.

clue.text: The debate is a feature after refreshment

indicators.note: after places the feature at the end, following the refreshment

parts.note: tea is a common refreshment
the chin is a facial feature

explanation.surface: A discussion that follows tea time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a feature' is a facial one, CHIN, coming after TEA.
explanation.definitionFit: A teach-in is an informal lecture and discussion session on a topical issue, a kind of debate.

clue.text: I allow in a politician in preparation for washing

indicators.note: in tells us to place I and the word for allow inside the politician

parts.note: a Tory is a British Conservative politician
to let is to allow

explanation.surface: Someone lets a Conservative join them while getting ready to bathe.
explanation.walkthrough: TORY, a British Conservative, is split as TO-RY to take I + LET.
explanation.definitionFit: A toiletry is a product such as soap or shampoo used when washing oneself.

clue.text: Where paints are mixed without poetry

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the jumbled paints surround the poetry
are mixed tells us the letters of paints are jumbled

parts.note: an ode is a piece of poetry

explanation.surface: A studio where an artist mixes colours away from verse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'are mixed' turns PAINTS into ANTIPS; 'without' means outside, so ANTIPS wraps ODE.
explanation.definitionFit: The antipodes are places diametrically opposite on the globe, a cryptic 'where'.

clue.text: Language which sends me after the deer

indicators.note: after puts the speaker following the deer

parts.note: a hind is a female deer
I is the speaker, me

explanation.surface: A tongue that sends someone chasing a deer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' sounds like a pursuit but simply places I after HIND.
explanation.definitionFit: Hindi is the principal official language of India.

clue.text: Plants of which the Queen got in numbers

indicators.note: got in tells us the royal letters enter the word for numbers

parts.note: nines are numbers
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: The monarch acquired a large quantity of flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: ER (Elizabeth Regina) goes inside NINES.
explanation.definitionFit: Nerines are South African bulbous flowering plants, such as the Guernsey lily.

clue.text: Strips a girl with undergarments

parts.note: Di is a girl's name, short for Diana
vests are undergarments in British use

explanation.surface: A young woman takes off her clothes down to her underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: In British English a vest is a sleeveless undershirt.
explanation.definitionFit: To divest is to strip or deprive someone of something.

clue.text: Chanter in the right about film actor

parts.note: taken as written
Franchot Tone was a Hollywood film actor
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A singer in the right concerning a movie star.
explanation.walkthrough: Franchot Tone was an American film star of the 1930s; 'about' here simply joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To intone is to chant in a monotone, so one who does it is a chanter.

clue.text: Member of an American sect who gives the saviour a theatre article

parts.note: Christ is the Saviour in Christian belief
the Adelphi is a theatre on the Strand in London
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A believer who credits the saviour with a playhouse and an item.
explanation.walkthrough: The Adelphi is a West End theatre in London.
explanation.definitionFit: The Christadelphians are a Bible-based religious community founded in the United States in the 1840s.

clue.text: Song which is wicked about everything

indicators.note: about means around, so the word for wicked surrounds the word for everything

parts.note: wicked means bad
everything is all

explanation.surface: A tune that is thoroughly evil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts BAD round ALL.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballad is a narrative poem or song, often sentimental.

clue.text: Military command concerning reputation

parts.note: about means concerning
face is reputation or standing, as in losing face

explanation.surface: An order on a parade ground about someone's good name.
explanation.definitionFit: About face is the drill order to turn round and face the opposite way.

clue.text: Puts on a play for a leader among professionals

indicators.note: among places the leader inside the professionals

parts.note: pros is short for professionals
Duce, Italian for leader, was Mussolini's title

explanation.surface: A director stages a show to serve a chief among experts.
explanation.walkthrough: Il Duce was Mussolini's title, so DUCE stands for a leader.
explanation.definitionFit: To produce a play is to stage it, to put it on.

clue.text: Port with means of lowering boats westward in it for time-keeping

indicators.note: in it tells us the lock and west go inside the port

parts.note: Cork is an Irish port
a canal lock raises and lowers boats
W stands for west

explanation.surface: A harbour with a canal lock to the west, used for keeping time.
explanation.walkthrough: CORK, the port in Ireland, takes LOCK + W inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Clockwork is the spring-driven mechanism used in clocks and watches to keep time.

clue.text: Burdens when one has to dispense a lot

parts.note: to pay is to dispense money
loads means a lot

explanation.surface: Weights to bear when someone must hand out a great deal.
explanation.definitionFit: A payload is the load carried by a vehicle, a burden it bears.

clue.text: Wrinkles one of which sounds genuine

clue.text: A little bit behind a fool in class

indicators.note: behind puts the scrap after the fool

parts.note: an ass is a fool
an ort is a scrap or fragment of food

explanation.surface: A small amount trails behind an idiot in school.
explanation.walkthrough: ORT, a scrap of food left over, is a crossword favourite; 'class' is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To assort is to sort into groups, to classify.

clue.text: Disturbance of the seas which may make one die during the journey

indicators.note: during places the rearranged letters inside the journey

parts.note: a trip is a journey

indicators.note: may make one says the letters of die can be formed into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A rough patch at sea that could be fatal on a voyage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may make one' rearranges DIE to IDE, which 'during' puts inside TRIP.
explanation.definitionFit: A tide-rip is rough water caused by opposing tides or currents meeting.

clue.text: Kind of energy which needs a male in charge

parts.note: a tom is a male cat

explanation.surface: A form of power that requires a man in control.
explanation.definitionFit: Atomic energy is energy released by nuclear reactions.

clue.text: Met when holding thanks back on food and replied

indicators.note: holding means the word for met contains the other pieces

parts.note: met an argument means countered it

indicators.note: back says the word for thanks is turned round

parts.note: ta is informal British for thanks
tack is slang for food, as in hard tack

explanation.surface: Faced while grasping gratitude backwards, someone hit back over a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns TA into AT; AT + TACK goes inside COUNTERED, split COUNTER-ED.
explanation.definitionFit: To counterattack is to respond to an attack with one's own, a forceful reply.

clue.text: A mule becomes exponents of the law

indicators.note: becomes signals the letters turning into something new

explanation.surface: A donkey-horse cross turns into legal experts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'becomes' rearranges A MULE.
explanation.definitionFit: The ulema are the body of Muslim scholars learned in Islamic law.

clue.text: Born first-class and senior

parts.note: A1 means first-class, written here as AI
nee means born, used of a woman's maiden name

explanation.surface: Born top quality and older.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 (first-class) is written AI; the pieces go in answer order though the clue gives Born first.
explanation.definitionFit: Aînée is French for the elder, applied to a sister or daughter.

clue.text: Young animal we blame wrongly

indicators.note: wrongly tells us the letters are put in the wrong order

explanation.surface: We unfairly accuse a young sheep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrongly' rearranges WE BLAME.
explanation.definitionFit: A ewe lamb is a young female sheep.

clue.text: Handsome city on a height

indicators.note: on in an across clue means the city follows the height

parts.note: Shap is a high fell and pass in Cumbria
Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire

explanation.surface: A good-looking city set on a hill.
explanation.walkthrough: Shap Fell is a high point in Cumbria; Ely is a small English cathedral city.
explanation.definitionFit: Shapely means well-formed, attractive in shape, so handsome.

clue.text: Medical examination when hell is in the prize

indicators.note: is in places the word for hell inside the prize

parts.note: a cup is a trophy, a prize
heck is a mild substitute for hell

explanation.surface: A doctor's look-over when hell breaks out at the trophy.
explanation.walkthrough: HECK, the mild oath, goes inside CUP.
explanation.definitionFit: A check-up is a routine medical examination.
